First up, this is not a kill switch. Second up, this isn't talking about hard A.I nor soft A.I. This won't help prevent a robot apocalypse, nor will skynet from the future ensure its future safety by sending robots back in time to kill this team off.

The whole "safe interruptability" thingy is required because A.I is incomplete or imperfect today. We are getting very good at building A.I systems that know how to do something (drive a car, pick up boxes, recognize dickbutt posts in Reddit...) but we don't know how to build A.I systems well that can decide what to do (Should I drive the car for this stretch? Should I avoid picking up this damaged box that might spill out? Can I ignore what appears to be this 2kb corrupted file, dickbutt.jpg that I have been attempting to recognize for 23hrs...)

While these imperfections exist, our only option is to allow a "human overwrite" of the system (Give me the car now, Skip this box, Ctrl + C ... ).

However, in many situations, human interruption can be indistinguishable from regular obstacles that an A.I has to overcome (indistinguishable because our A.I systems are not perfect).

A.I systems constantly improve their skills by learning. What Google is working on is how to stop the A.I from picking up bad-habits by attempting to learn from human intervention (Don't learn to hand over control in these types of road, Don't learn to avoid picking up pink boxes, Don't learn to avoid files that are called dickbutt.jpg...)

That's what they mean by "safe interruptability" - how to safely interrupt a learning process without teaching it that being interrupted is a good thing for some tasks.
